org: NS (Nederlandse Spoorwegen / Dutch Railways) — Tractie Design System
accessNotes: The zeroheight page is JS-rendered (web_fetch failed with a transport error; curl returned only the app shell), so it was rendered in a headless browser and the article text and all 14 example images were extracted. The guide only names palette tokens ({color.palette.blue.600} etc.); exact hex values were read from the CSS custom properties (--tractie-color-chart-category-1 ...) shipped by the public Tractie Storybook (@tractie/styles), for both :root (light) and [data-color-scheme="dark"]. Typography tokens (Roboto) also read from Storybook CSS. The @tractie/tokens npm package could not be reached from this environment.
summary: Product-UI design system for NS internal employee applications (dashboards, tools). Charts are calm and functional: Roboto, a dark-blue first series (#0C44A1), a fixed 8-colour categorical order tuned for 3:1 contrast in light and dark mode, light grey gridlines, a grey baseline, small rounded bar ends, white gaps between adjacent colours and legend below the chart. Tractie provides guidelines and a Figma bar-chart reference but no coded chart components.

colors.categoricalNotes: Tokens color.chart.category-1..8 = palette blue.600, teal.400, yellow.700, pink.600, purple.400, teal.600, yellow.900, pink.400 (light). 'Don't reorder these colors, since they are in an optimized sequence for contrast and accessibility.' Limit categories to 5 ('Be aware that having more then 5 categories could make a chart more difficult to read'). Start with a single colour - use color.chart.category-1 for single-colour charts; only use categorical colours when they add meaning. Dark mode values: #9AC5F1, #2B87A6, #FED652, #F6A2CF, #885DD0, #8DD9EC, #FFF2C8, #D53483.
colors.notes: Semantic chart tokens (light / dark): color.chart.neutral #919197 / #75767C ('Use to tone down elements'); color.chart.success #3E9D7B / #47BD99; color.chart.warning #F05C00 / #FF9544; color.chart.error #CE092D / #EB0F38. Categorical palette avoids semantic red/green/orange to prevent confusion. Unfilled remainder of a part (e.g. donut track) uses color.background.accent.gray.subtle #060F2E1C (dark #FFFFFF29) - 'does not pass 3:1 contrast ratio. Do not use it for communicating data.' Guide says use border tokens for axes and content tokens for text: gridline/axis hexes above are the border.default (#060F2E1C, alpha) and border.emphasis (#00021B3B) tokens - which border token maps to grid vs baseline is an inference from the anatomy image (light grey grid, darker grey baseline). Text: content.default #252528, content.subtle #00010D8C (axis labels appear mid-grey). Dark mode: background.default #0D0E10, elevated-1 #191A1C, elevated-2 #252528, content.default #C4C5CB, border.default #FFFFFF29. All categorical and semantic colours pass 3:1 against all elevation backgrounds in light and dark mode. Focus/interactive blue #0062D1.

axisTitle.placement: y title rotated 90° next to the y labels; x title centred below the x labels (both optional)

typography.notes: Type tokens: family 'Roboto, sans-serif'; sizes xs .75rem, s .875rem, m 1rem, l clamp(1-1.125rem), xl clamp(1.125-1.25rem), xxl clamp(1.25-1.5rem); weights 400/500/700; leading 1, 1.25, 1.5. Title/axis sizes above are estimates read from the anatomy image (title rendered in dark navy, similar to content.emphasis #0A3680; axis labels in subtle grey) - not stated numerically in the guide. Chart title is optional and 'Describes the chart in a short sentence' (example 'X per maand').

structure.gridlines: Light grey solid lines along the value axis only (horizontal for column charts, vertical for horizontal bar charts).
structure.axisLine: Baseline (zero line) drawn as a slightly darker grey line; no separate value-axis line.
structure.zeroLine: 'Baseline: The zero-point on the axis from which bars grow' - darker grey than gridlines. Most charts start Y at zero; non-zero baselines acceptable mainly for line charts showing shape of change.
structure.yAxisTitle: optional; rotated, beside the y-axis labels
structure.unitPlacement: In axis labels ('Explains what data is being shown on each axis and in what units'), e.g. 0% 25% 50% 75%.
structure.frame: None within the chart; charts sit on product surfaces (elevated backgrounds).
structure.background: Inherits UI background: #FFFFFF light (elevated-1/2 also #FFF), #0D0E10/#191A1C/#252528 dark.
structure.notes: Use consistent, clear and simple intervals.

legend.directLabels: Recommended as an extra cue alongside shapes/line patterns ('use other visual indicators like shapes, line patterns or direct labels').
legend.title: none
legend.notes: 'Do not include a legend for single-category charts. Be aware that legends may not be accessible for users with color blindness. Tooltips should be provided as an additional cue.'

marks.bars: Bar width 16px with at least 8px spacing between bars; never below 16px width / 8px spacing. Grouped bars: 12px width, 2px between bars within a group, at least 16px between groups. Outer end of bars slightly rounded (small radius); stacked segments separated by a thin white gap. Use horizontal bars when bars exceed available width or labels are long.
marks.lines: Medium-weight lines (~2-3px) with a distinct marker shape per series (circle, diamond, square, triangle) so colour is not the only cue.
marks.areas: Suggested as an alternative to increase data density instead of thinner bars.
marks.pies: Donut/ring gauges shown for single percentages: thick ring in category-1 with the remainder in accent.gray.subtle, rounded ends and a gap between segments, big bold value and label centred.
marks.notes: Separate adjacent colours with a border or gap - chart colours don't pass 3:1 against each other.

labels.dates: Abbreviated month names on the category axis (Jan, Feb, Mar).
labels.notes: Product UI is Dutch-language (example title 'X per maand').

furniture.title: Optional chart title describing the chart in a short sentence, above the plot, left-aligned.

annotations: Highlight an interesting data point by toning down less important data with color.chart.neutral (#919197).
layout: Bar density rules fix bar width/spacing in px (16/8, grouped 12/2/16), so chart width scales with bar count; switch to horizontal or area chart rather than shrinking bars.
interaction: Tooltips should be provided as an additional cue alongside the legend. Focus/interactive tokens: border.focus #0062D1 (dark #5D9FEA). Tractie supplies no coded chart components - teams style their own library with Tractie tokens.
accessibility: All categorical and semantic colours pass 3:1 against all elevation backgrounds in light and dark mode; separate colours by a border or gap; never rely on colour alone - use shapes, line patterns or direct labels ('you have to be able to understand a data visualisation even when it's in black and white'); semantic colours always need a secondary cue (icon/label).

chartTypes.notes: Figma Bar Chart component provided as reference.

distinctiveRules.rule: Fixed categorical order: #0C44A1 dark blue, #33A0C4 teal, #B69016 ochre, #BE2771 magenta-pink, #A880EF lilac, #236D86 dark teal, #6A5618 olive-brown, #EA66AA pink; never reorder.
distinctiveRules.quote: Don't reorder these colors, since they are in an optimized sequence for contrast and accessibility.

distinctiveRules.rule: Single-series charts use only color.chart.category-1 (#0C44A1); no rainbow bars.
distinctiveRules.quote: Use color.chart.category-1 for single color charts.

distinctiveRules.rule: Separate adjacent colours (stacked segments, donut segments) with a white gap/border.
distinctiveRules.quote: Separate chart colors by a border or gap.

distinctiveRules.rule: Bar width 16px with ≥8px spacing; grouped bars 12px wide, 2px inside groups, ≥16px between groups.
distinctiveRules.quote: Set bar width to 16px, with at least 8px of spacing between bars.

distinctiveRules.rule: Legend below the chart, left-aligned, with rounded-square swatches; no legend for single-category charts; tooltips as additional cue.
distinctiveRules.quote: Do not include a legend for single-category charts ... Tooltips should be provided as an additional cue.

distinctiveRules.rule: Line series each get a distinct marker shape (circle, diamond, square, triangle) so charts read in black and white.
distinctiveRules.quote: Make sure to use other visual indicators like shapes, line patterns or direct labels.

distinctiveRules.rule: Highlight by greying out: non-focus data in color.chart.neutral #919197.
distinctiveRules.quote: Highlight an interesting data point by toning down less important data in a chart with color.chart.neutral.

distinctiveRules.rule: Semantic chart colours reserved for meaning: success #3E9D7B, warning #F05C00, error #CE092D; kept out of the categorical palette.
distinctiveRules.quote: We avoid those colors within the categorical chart colors to prevent confusion.

distinctiveRules.rule: Full dark-mode palette swap via tokens (category-1 becomes #9AC5F1, background #0D0E10), every chart colour keeping ≥3:1 contrast on all elevations.
distinctiveRules.quote: These colors also pass 3:1 color contrast ratios on all elevated backgrounds in light and dark mode.

distinctiveRules.rule: Light grey gridlines along the value axis only, a darker grey zero baseline, no tick marks; grey Roboto axis labels.
distinctiveRules.quote: Anatomy: Grid lines ... Baseline: The zero-point on the axis from which bars grow.

distinctiveRules.rule: Bars have slightly rounded outer ends (top of the stack only).
distinctiveRules.quote: Observed in the stacked column and horizontal bar example images

distinctiveRules.rule: Unfilled remainder of a progress/donut uses accent.gray.subtle and must never encode data.
distinctiveRules.quote: Use color.accent.gray.subtle when part of a graph is not filled ... Do not use it for communicating data.

referenceImages.describes: Anatomy diagram on a very light grey canvas: chart title 'X per maand' top-left in medium-weight dark navy Roboto (~20px). Stacked column chart with dark blue (#0C44A1) bottom segments and teal (#33A0C4) tops separated by a thin white line; tops slightly rounded. Light grey horizontal gridlines at 1-4; slightly darker grey baseline at 0; y labels grey on the left; rotated 'Y title' beside them; month labels (Jan-Mar) below and 'X title' centred under them. No ticks or axis lines. Legend below the chart, left-aligned, with rounded-square swatches and 'Label' text.

Line chart on white, four series each with a distinct filled marker: dark blue circles, teal diamonds, ochre squares, magenta triangles; lines ~2-3px. Light grey horizontal gridlines at 25%/50%/75%, grey baseline at 0%; y labels grey percentages left; month labels Jan-Jun below; no legend, no ticks.

Horizontal stacked bar chart: four bars (Jan-Apr) with dark blue, teal and ochre segments separated by white gaps, outer right end slightly rounded. Light grey vertical gridlines at 0-4, darker grey vertical baseline at 0; grey category labels right-aligned left of the baseline; grey value labels below; generous spacing between bars.

Progress donut: thick dark blue ring for 75% with rounded ends and small gaps, remainder in very light grey (color.background.accent.gray.subtle); centre shows bold '75%' and 'Coverage' in Roboto; a token callout above.
